Prepare length composition data for model input

prep_lf_data.Rd

Transforms wide or long length-frequency observations (one composition per fishery x timestep and optional source) into model-ready arrays and vectors that opal_model and get_length_like expect. The function validates bin alignment against the length structure in data, optionally filters to a subset of fisheries, and appends every derived object directly to data.

Usage

prep_lf_data(
  data,
  lf_wide,
  lf_keep_fisheries = NULL,
  lf_switch = 1L,
  lf_minbin = NULL,
  lf_maxbin = NULL,
  lf_var_adjust = NULL,
  lf_cap = NULL,
  lf_addtocomp = 1e-08,
  lf_upper_edge = NULL,
  lf_tails = c("accumulate", "truncate"),
  lf_edge_tol = 1e-08 * data$len_bin_width,
  lf_allow_misaligned = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

a list containing at minimum the length structure scalars len_bin_start, len_bin_width, n_len, and n_fishery.

lf_wide

A wide data frame, list of wide data frames, or long data frame. Wide frames contain fishery, year, month, ts, and numeric count columns named by bin lower edges. Long input contains the same metadata plus bin_lower, bin_upper, and count. Long observations are grouped by fishery, ts, and optionally source; calendar metadata is taken from the first row.

lf_keep_fisheries

integer vector of fishery indices to retain. Pass NULL (the default) to keep all fisheries present in lf_wide.

lf_switch

integer likelihood type selector passed straight through to data$lf_switch (1 = multinomial, 2 = Dirichlet, 3 = Dirichlet-multinomial). Default 1L.

lf_minbin

integer vector length n_fishery giving the minimum bin index (1-based) used for each fishery. Defaults to rep(1L, n_fishery).

lf_maxbin

integer vector length n_fishery giving the maximum bin index (1-based) used for each fishery. Defaults to rep(n_len, n_fishery).

lf_var_adjust

numeric vector of length n_fishery used to scale the effective sample size for each fishery. For observation row \(i\) belonging to fishery \(f\), the sample size is adjusted as \(n_i / \text{lf\_var\_adjust}_f\). Values greater than 1 downweight (reduce effective \(N\)) and values less than 1 upweight the fishery. Defaults to rep(1, n_fishery) (no adjustment).

lf_cap

positive integer (or NULL). When supplied, each effective sample size is capped: \(n_i = \min(n_i, \text{lf\_cap})\). Applied after proportions are computed so that observed compositions are unaffected. Default NULL (no cap). This is a Multifan-CL legacy feature.

lf_addtocomp

small non-negative numeric constant added to observed composition proportions after tail compression and before renormalisation. This robustifies zero bins. Default 1e-08.

lf_upper_edge

Final upper edge, or one per element of a list of wide data frames. Defaults to the model length-grid upper edge, data$len_bin_start + data$n_len * data$len_bin_width. Ignored for long input, which supplies both boundaries explicitly.

lf_tails

Prediction tail handling: "accumulate" (default) extends the outer matrix edges, or "truncate" excludes outside mass.

lf_edge_tol

Absolute edge tolerance; defaults to 1e-8 * data$len_bin_width. Nearby model edges snap silently.

lf_allow_misaligned

Allow observed edges to split model bins, with a diagnostic warning. The default rejects all edges not matching a model boundary, including edges beyond the model range.

Value

The input data list with the following elements appended or updated:

len_lower, len_upper, len_mid

Length bin boundary and midpoint vectors derived from the scalar inputs.

lf_switch

Passed through from the argument.

lf_obs_in

Observed proportions in retained input order: a matrix with one row per observation when bin counts agree, otherwise a list of row vectors. Native input has n_len columns.

lf_n

Numeric vector of sample sizes per observation row.

lf_n_int

Integer Dirichlet-multinomial sample sizes obtained by half-up rounding of lf_n.

lf_fishery

Integer vector of fishery index per observation row.

lf_fishery_f

Integer vector of unique fishery indices with LF data.

lf_n_f

Integer vector of observation counts per fishery.

lf_year

Integer vector of model timestep index (1-based) per observation row.

lf_year_fi, lf_n_fi, lf_n_int_fi, lf_row_fi

Lists split by fishery containing model timesteps, effective sample sizes, and row indices. Precomputed so opal_model() does not rebuild them on every objective evaluation.

lf_season

Integer vector of season index (all 1).

lf_minbin, lf_maxbin

Passed through from arguments.

lf_var_adjust

Passed through from argument; numeric vector [n_fishery] of variance-adjustment divisors applied to lf_n.

removal_switch_f

Integer vector [n_fishery] of removal flags (all 0).

n_lf

Total number of observation rows.

lf_obs_data

Named list list(obs = lf_obs_list) for plain-R access in get_length_like.

lf_obs_flat

Flattened numeric vector of counts (for multinomial, lf_switch = 1).

lf_obs_ints

Flattened integer counts that sum to lf_n_int per observation (for Dirichlet-multinomial, lf_switch = 3).

lf_obs_prop

Flattened numeric vector of normalised proportions (for Dirichlet, lf_switch = 2).

lf_addtocomp

Stored value of the add-to-composition constant used to robustify observed composition bins.

lf_nbins

Legacy scalar bin count for the first observation in fishery-grouped flat order, or zero for empty input. Use lf_nbins_i for heterogeneous observations.

Details

Inputs may also be lists of wide data frames or long data frames. Observed counts remain on their original grid. lf_scheme_edges is a deduplicated list of observed edges, including native min/max pooling. lf_rebin_s contains prediction matrices (observed bins by model length bins). lf_scheme and lf_nbins_i follow fishery-grouped flat observation order, while lf_row_fi indexes retained input order. The logical lf_native_i, in flat observation order, identifies observations originally on the full native grid before min/max pooling. Heterogeneous observations use lists instead of rectangular matrices.

Splitting a model length bin at an observed boundary assumes uniform prediction mass within that model bin. This approximation is not needed when observed boundaries match model boundaries, so nonmatching boundaries are rejected by default. Setting lf_allow_misaligned = TRUE opts into the approximation with a diagnostic warning. Check bin labeling and units before changing the grid. Diagnostics suggest a finer width dividing the observed offsets; edges beyond the model range also require extending that range. Changing the grid changes the mean and SD of len_mid, which scale length-based selectivity parameters: existing par_sel values are not directly transferable.

Observations with a total sample size of zero are silently removed after validating counts and edges. Bin alignment against the model's length structure is checked with the edge tolerance. Dirichlet-multinomial counts use half-up rounding of effective sample sizes and largest-remainder allocation. Observations that round to zero are skipped by the Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood.
